title: Blueprint Trace — OMA Construction Draft
description: A monospace-only, all-caps architectural template structured like a live construction document: dimension lines bracket the slide edges, orthographic wireframes anchor the layout, and warm trace-paper cream distinguishes it from sterile digital blueprints.
philosophy: This template exists because most architecture presentations apologize for their discipline — drowning rigor in glossy renders and lifestyle photography. It refuses that bargain entirely, treating every slide as a technical document where the drawing is the argument and annotation is the only permitted color. Modeled on the analytical site-analysis pages of OMA and Herzog & de Meuron, it is built for practitioners who believe a proposal earns credibility through precision, not production value. Decoration is not restrained here; it is structurally excluded.
goodFor: Architecture firm building proposals and urban-planning competition briefs
Site analysis and zoning presentations anchored by orthographic section drawings
Academic design reviews at schools of architecture requiring technical legibility
Urban-strategy decks where annotated diagrams carry more weight than imagery
avoidFor: Consumer-facing marketing or retail brand launches requiring photographic warmth
Chart-heavy quarterly business reviews that depend on multi-color data encoding
Pitches to general audiences unfamiliar with construction-drawing conventions
Campaigns where lifestyle renders or mood imagery are the primary narrative device
author: harness

examples.promptCore: The slide feels like the title sheet of a live working drawing set — authoritative, unapologetic, structured entirely by annotation logic. An orthographic section or axonometric ghost anchors the visual field, present not as decoration but as proof of rigor. Text arrives as stamped notation: sparse, all-caps, institutionally confident, with nothing present that isn't load-bearing. The mood is warm drafting-table intensity — trace paper under a lamp, not a screen — avoiding softness, gradient warmth, or production gloss that would domesticate the discipline.

examples.layoutNotes: 12-column grid with dimension-line rules tick-marked to all four slide edges, forming a live measurement frame around the entire composition. Title block occupies the lower-left zone spanning roughly half the columns, anchored by a bold horizontal rule that reads as a dimension baseline rather than a decorative divider. A large orthographic wireframe — plan, section, or axonometric — fills the upper-right quadrant as the primary visual element, uncolored and structurally unadorned. Sheet metadata (project identifier, date, revision tag) runs in a tight row along the top-left margin; sheet number sits bottom-right, completing the construction-document header/footer convention.

examples.promptCore: The slide reads as a live construction document mid-annotation: an orthographic wireframe dominates the left field while a disciplined column of all-caps callouts occupies the right margin, connected by leader lines. Mood is austere and analytical, evoking OMA site-analysis pages where every mark earns its place through function alone. Composition is asymmetric — the wireframe zone breathes while the annotation column is tightly modular. Avoid gradients, decorative borders, or representational imagery.

examples.layoutNotes: 12-column grid; cols 1–7 form a wireframe-and-diagram zone bleeding to the left edge, while cols 8–12 hold a stacked annotation column with thin rule-line dividers mimicking a construction title block. Horizontal dimension lines with tick-mark terminals bracket the full top and bottom slide edges. The primary content label sits flush at the top of the annotation column in all-caps; sub-callouts stack below, optionally linked to the wireframe by leader lines. Page number and document-code stamp anchor the bottom-right corner; no decorative header band.
